transcript.text: My Samsung dishwasher DW60M6050FS keeps showing 4C and beeping, won't do anything

## What 4C Means

On Samsung dishwashers, 4C is a water supply error. The dishwasher isn't getting enough water within the expected time, so it stops and beeps. The cause is usually simple.

## Step 1: Stop the Beeping and Reset

1. Press and hold Start (or Power) for about 3 seconds to cancel, or turn it off.
2. For a full reset, switch off the circuit breaker (or unplug it) for 10–15 minutes, then restore power.

If the problem that caused the error is still there, the code will come back, so check the following.

## Step 2: Check the Water Supply (Most Common Causes)

Is the water valve fully open?
• Look under the kitchen sink for the shut-off valve feeding the dishwasher (usually on the hot water line). Make sure it's turned fully on (counterclockwise).
• This is very common after plumbing work or a new install.

Is there water and good pressure in the house?
• Run the hot tap at the kitchen sink. If the flow is weak or there's no water (supply work, frozen pipes in cold weather), the dishwasher will throw 4C.

Is the inlet hose kinked or crushed?
• Check behind and under the dishwasher, especially if it was recently pushed back into place.

## Step 3: Clean the Inlet Filter (Very Common Fix)

There's a small mesh screen where the water supply hose connects to the dishwasher's inlet valve. It often clogs with sediment or debris.

1. Turn off power at the breaker and shut off the water valve.
2. Remove the lower kick panel (toe plate) at the bottom front of the dishwasher. It's usually held by a couple of screws.
3. Put a towel and shallow pan down, then disconnect the water supply line from the inlet valve.
4. Inspect the mesh screen inside the connection. Rinse or gently pick out debris.
5. Reconnect firmly, turn the water on, check for leaks, and restore power.

## Step 4: Check the Drain Hose Setup

If the drain hose doesn't have a high loop (raised up under the counter) or is pushed too far into the drain pipe, water can siphon out as fast as it fills. The machine never reaches the right level and shows 4C. Make sure the hose loops up to the underside of the counter.

## Step 5: If It Still Shows 4C

If water supply, pressure, filter, and hoses are all fine, the likely culprits are:
• Faulty water inlet valve. It may not open even when it gets power. This is a common replacement part.
• Flow meter or sensor fault.
• Control board issue (less common).

At this point it's worth contacting Samsung Support or an appliance technician. If the dishwasher is under warranty, call Samsung before opening anything major.

---

Quick question to help narrow it down: When you start a cycle, do you hear water running into the machine at all, or is it completely silent? And was anything recently changed, like plumbing work, a move, or the unit being pulled out?
It's completely silent, no water noise at all. A plumber fitted a new kitchen tap yesterday and it's been doing this since, he was working under the sink.

That timing makes the cause almost certain. Complete silence (no water noise at all) means no water is reaching the dishwasher. When plumbers work under the sink, they routinely shut off the dishwasher's supply and sometimes forget to turn it back on.

## 1. Check the Dishwasher Isolation Valve (Most Likely Fix)

Under the sink, follow the dishwasher's inlet hose (usually grey or white) back to where it screws onto the pipework. There should be a small valve there, often with a blue or red lever.

• Lever type: Lever in line with the pipe = ON. Lever across the pipe = OFF. Turn it so it lines up with the pipe.
• Slotted screw type: Turn the slot so it's in line with the pipe, using a flat screwdriver.

Then cancel the error (hold Power, or switch off at the wall for a minute) and start a cycle. You should hear water within a few seconds.

## 2. If the Valve Is On, Check These

• Kinked or trapped hose: The hose may have been bent or crushed by tools, the new tap's flexible pipes, or items put back in the cupboard. Straighten it out.
• Hose actually connected? Occasionally the dishwasher hose gets disconnected or the outlet gets capped during the work. Make sure it's screwed onto a live supply.

## 3. Blocked Inlet Filter (Common After Water Was Shut Off)

When the mains is turned off and back on, sediment can get flushed through and clog the small mesh filter.

1. Turn off the isolation valve and put a towel and bowl down.
2. Unscrew the inlet hose from the valve under the sink.
3. Look inside the hose end for a small mesh screen. Rinse it out under a tap.
4. Reconnect hand-tight plus a little more, turn the valve on, and check for drips.

## 4. Still Nothing?

Call the plumber back. Since it stopped working right after his job, he should sort it at no charge. It will almost certainly be a quick fix for him.

One more thing to check once water is flowing: If he fitted a new sink waste or trap, make sure the dishwasher drain hose is pushed back onto its spigot. New waste kits often have a sealed blanking cap on that spigot that needs cutting off. If it's still sealed, you'll get a drain error next instead.
Found it. The screwdriver-slot valve under the sink was at 90 degrees, so it was turned off. I turned it in line with the pipe and the dishwasher now fills and runs normally.

That was the cause, then. The plumber shut it off to work on the tap and forgot to turn it back on.

While this first cycle runs, it's worth a quick look under the sink for:

• Drips around the valve and hose connections, since things were disturbed.
• The drain hose, to make sure it's still firmly connected to the sink waste or trap. If the plumber changed that, look for leaks there when the dishwasher pumps out, usually a few minutes into the cycle and again at the end.

If everything stays dry, you're all set.
